summary: Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dza Pukhung Tulku Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught numerous students, including Sogyal Rinpoche and Keith Dowman.

Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Mindrolling and Dorje Drak monasteries under teachers including Sera Khandro and Khenpo Aten, taught widely, and founded the International Nyingma Society.

Dugald Mackichan (1851–1932) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Glasgow, University of Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as Principal of Wilson College, Mumbai (1878–1920) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1888–1890).

Duncan Forbes (1798–1868) worked in linguistics and Indology after studying at Perth Grammar School and the University of St Andrews. He taught at Calcutta Academy (1823–1826) and served as Professor of Oriental languages at King's College London (1837–1861).

Duncan Ryūken Williams (born 1969) specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Reed College and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held posts at Harvard, UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.
Dung Ngoc Duong works in Buddhist studies and religious studies, completing a PhD at Boston University in 2001 under the supervision of Malcolm David Eckel.

Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle (1927–1997) studied at Trashichöling, Sera, and Gyuto monasteries under Ngawang Yönten and Tsadru Ngawang Losang. A Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, he held professorships at Minzu University of China and Tibet University.

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He held professorships at Narasinha Dutt College, Scottish Church College (1928–1952), and Sanskrit College and University (1952).
Durga Prasad Dikshit, a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, earned his PhD at the University of Lucknow. He studied under Baij Nath Puri, R. K. Dikshit, and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi.
Dušan Zbavitel (1925–2012) was an Indologist who studied at Charles University (1945–1949) under Vincenc Lesný and later held a post at the same university.

Dwarikadas Shastri (born 1922) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He founded Bauddha Bharati and served as co-editor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Dwight Whitney Learned (1848–1943) worked in religious studies and Japanology. He earned his BA and PhD at Yale University under William Dwight Whitney, taught at Thayer College (1872–1875), and was a professor at Doshisha University (1875–1928).
Dwijendra Narayan Jha (1940–2021) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Presidency University, Patna University, and the University of Calcutta.

Dylan Esler works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at SOAS and earned his PhD from KU Leuven, where he was a research scholar. He also held posts at Ruhr University Bochum and 84000: Translating the Words of the Buddha.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche (born 1964) is an active scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and Khenpo Rinchen, and taught at Naropa University in 1990.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (born 1965) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University, and served as director of the Nitartha Institute and Kamalashila Institute.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche (born 1961) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS, learning under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, and Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.
Dániel Balogh works in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 2021) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).
Dávid Jónás works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD in 2019 at Eötvös Loránd University and became an assistant lecturer there in 2021.
